scope: Native worksheet/workbook/range protection and Allow Edit Ranges only. Existing encrypted-file reader remains reachable through Workbooks.Open Password. No new protection algorithm, encryption writer, protected-view graph, IRM/user ACL service, certificate store or native named-style inclusion mode.

required_obligations.profile: Live typed Protection/AllowEditRanges/AllowEditRange nodes over native state. One-based/default/title lookup, bounded enumeration, same-workbook/receiver-sheet Range Add, read-only Range, Title rename, ChangePassword, Delete and session Unprotect all use existing commands. Native lifetime tokens survive COW/undo/rename and never persist to files or affect content equality. Definition edits revoke prior matching native grants, preventing password-change/delete-recreate bypass. Names use a 255-byte trimmed nonempty input profile; passwords are bounded to 1024 bytes and never retained as text in handles or journals. Up to 8192 children and 64 areas; AllowEdit checks at most 65536 cells using the same native policy as edits, returning False if any is blocked. AllowEdit is content editability, not permission to format/insert/delete. Import securityDescriptor bytes remain opaque and are not presented as ACL enforcement. Deleting an owner sheet revokes its grants; undo restores definitions but never resurrects revoked authentication.

Existing High protection paths stay live. Worksheet Protect/Unprotect require method invocation; unsupported independent Contents/DrawingObjects/Scenarios and UI-only/insert-hyperlinks/pivot-table permissions still refuse before effects. Permission getters expose native stored flags; unsupported grant flags and ProtectionMode are False. ProtectDrawingObjects/ProtectScenarios reflect the existing worksheet guard, not independent switches. EnableSelection projects stored protected-sheet flags with an atomic selectionOnly native command parameter that preserves the password and all other rights; setting while unprotected refuses because native has no dormant selection preference. Native locked-only selection has no XlEnableSelection value and refuses the getter. Failed authentication keeps protection and grants unchanged. XLSX persists hashes/options/ranges but never session unlocks. Workbook structure protection and document trust remain separate from file encryption or IRM.
